questions.question: What day would it be on 1 September 2020?
questions.solution:
Number of odd days in 2000 years = 0

Number of odd days in 19 years = (4 leap years + 15 ordinary years) = (4 × 2 + 15) = 23

23 odd days = (3 weeks + 2 days) = 2 odd days

1 January 2020 to 1 September 2020 = (31 + 29 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 1) = 245 odd days

245 odd days = (35 weeks) = 0 odd days

Therefore total odd days = 2

Hence on 1st September 2020 it will be Tuesday.

questions.question: {{If}} {a²} + (1)/({{a²)}} = 3, {{then}} {a³} + (1)/({{a³)}} = ?
questions.solution:
⇒ a² + 1/a² = 3

⇒ (a + 1/a)² = a² + 1/a² + 2

⇒ (a + 1/a)² = 3 + 2 = 5

⇒ (a + 1/a) = √5

∴ (a³ + 1/a³) = (a + 1/a)(a² – 1 + 1/a²) = (√5)(3 – 1) = 2√5

Thus, the correct answer is option **2.**

questions.question: A can work twice as fast as B. A and C together can work thrice as fast as B. If A, B and C complete a job in 30 days working together, in how many days can each of them complete the work?
questions.solution:
A, B and C complete a job in 30 days working together,

⇒ 1/A + 1/B + 1/C = 1/30

A can work twice as fast as B,

⇒ 1/B = 1/2A

A and C together can work thrice as fast as B,

⇒ 1/B = 1/3(1/A + 1/C)

Solving,

⇒ 3/B = 1/A + 1/C

⇒ 3/B = 1/30 – 1/B

⇒ 1/B = 120

Then,

⇒ 1/A = 1/60

⇒ 1/C = 1/120

∴ A, B and C can complete work in 60, 120 and 120 days respectively.

questions.question: A source maintains a current I in a resistor of resistance R. If V is the potential difference across the resistor, the electrical energy dissipated in the resistor in time t is given by _____.
questions.solution:
• Current in the resistor = I
 
• The resistance of the resistor = R
 
• The voltage of the resistor = V
 
• The time during which energy dissipated = t
 
• According to the ohms law, we get resistance R = V/I.
 
• The energy dissipated in the resistance is in the form of Heat.
 
• We know that H = I²Rt

 H = I² (V/I) t

 H = VIt

 
• The energy dissipated in the form of heat H = VIt Joules.

questions.question: If the electronic configuration of element A’ and B’ are 1s², 2s²2p⁶, 3s¹ and 1s²,2s²2p⁶,3s², 3p⁴ respectively, then the formula of the compound formed by the combination of these elements will be:
questions.solution:
• Given electronic configuration of element A’ is 1s², 2s²2p⁶, 3s¹.
 
• By solving the sub-orbital shells, we get (2 + 2 + 6 + 1) = 11.
 
• Therefore, the element with atomic number 11 is Sodium (Na).
 
• Given electronic configuration of element B’ is 1s²,2s²2p⁶,3s² ,3p⁴.
 
• By solving the sub-orbital shells, we get (2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4) = 16.
 
• Therefore, the element with atomic number 16 is Sulphur (S).
 
• The combination of A’B’, the compound we get will be A₂B.
 
• This is because 2 sodium atoms, each will lose 1 electron to achieve electron configuration of Neon and Sulphur will gain to 2 to get the configuration of Argon.
 
• A compound formed by Sodium and Sulphur will be Na₂S or Sodium Sulphide.

Consider the given statement and decide which of the given assumption/s is/are implicit.

**Statement:**

Serials/soaps are a reason for developing negative tendencies in women.

**Assumptions:**

I: Newspapers highlight the negative aspects first and then, the positive aspects.

II: The attention given to the negative aspects is much higher than that given to the positive aspects.

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are implicit
None of the assumptions are implicit.

questions.solution:
As the statement says that most of the serials or soap operas promote negative tendencies, the reason behind it can be assumed to be that ‘the attention given to the negative aspects is much higher than that given to the positive aspects’, hence assumption 2 is implicit.

As there is no information provided in the statement regarding the newspapers, we cannot assume anything about them. Hence, assumption 1 is not implicit.

questions.question: A sump is filled by three tankers with uniform flow. The first two tankers operating simultaneously fill the sump in the same time during which the sump is filled by the third tanker alone. The second tanker fills the sump 5 hours faster than the first tanker and 4 hours slower than the third tanker. The time required by the first tanker is:
questions.solution:
Let first tanker alone takes A hours to fill the sump.

Then second and third tanker will take (A – 5) and (A – 9) hours respectively.

⇒ 1/A + 1/ (A – 5) = 1/ (A – 9)

⇒ (2A – 5)(A – 9) = (A – 5)A

⇒ A² – 18A + 45 = 0

⇒ (A – 15)(A – 3) = 0

⇒ A = 15hours

∴ Time taken by first tanker = 15 hrs

questions.question:
Read the following question and decide which of the given statements is/are sufficient.

In a class of 51 students, how many girls scored above 80% in Maths?

**Statements: **

1. Exactly four boys scored above 80% in Maths.

2. One-third of the class scored above 80% in Maths.

options.text: Both 1 and 2 together are sufficient to answer the question.
2 alone is sufficient while 1 alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
1 alone is sufficient while 2 alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
Either 1 or 2 is sufficient to answer the question.

questions.solution:
Total students = 50

**Statement 2:**

Number of students scored 80% above = 51 × 1/3 = 17

As a specific number of boys is not unknown so we cannot find the number of girls.

**Statement 1:**

Number of boys scored 80% above = 4

From statement 1 and 2, number of girls that scored above 80% marks in maths = 17 - 4 = 13.

∴ Both 1 and 2 together are sufficient to answer the question.

questions.question: Type 1 workers are 2.5 times efficient than Type 2 workers. Twelve Type 1 workers can complete a task in 10 days. How many days would be taken 4 Type 1 and 15 Type 2 workers to do the same work?
questions.solution:
Given,

Twelve Type1 workers completed in 10 days.

⇒ One Type 1 worker will complete in 12 × 10 = 120 days

Type 1 worker are 2.5 time as efficient as Type 2 workers,

⇒ One type 2 worker complete in = 2.5 × 120 = 300 days

⇒ One Type 1 worker 1 day's work = 1/120

⇒ One type 2 worker 1 day’s work = 1/300

⇒ Four Type 1 workers and fifteen type 2 workers will complete work in = 4 × 1/120 + 15 × 1/300 = 1/30 + 1/20 = 1/12

∴ It will take 12 days to complete the work.

⇒ Length of the other diagonal = (24 × 2) /8

⇒ Length of the other diagonal = 6

(Side of rhombus)² = (half of one diagonal)² + (half of other diagonal)²

⇒ (Side of rhombus)² = 3² + 4²

∴ Side of rhombus = 5 m

questions.question: An echo is returned in 3 s. What is the distance of the reflecting surface from the source, considering the speed of sound as 342 ms⁻¹?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Echo: If we shout or clap near a suitable reflecting object such as a tall building or a mountain, we will hear the same sound again a little later. This sound which we hear is called an echo.

 
 
• Echoes are heard due to the phenomenon of Reflection of sound waves.
 
• To hear the echo clearly, the reflecting object must be more than 17.2 m from the sound source for the echo to be heard by a person standing at the source.
 
 

**Calculation:**__

Given that,

 An echo is returned after time (t) = 3s

Speed of the sound (v) = 342 m/s

Now according to the law's of motion distance traveled by sound waves can be given as 

Distance travelled (d) = v x t

 = 342 × 3

 = 1026m

Distance covered by the sound will double, as the sound will have to travel and source to reflecting surface and back from it hence distance will be ‘d’ is ‘2d.

 
• Now replacing ‘d’ with ‘2d’ we get

 2d = 1026

 d = 513 m

 
• The distance from the reflecting surface to the source is 513 m.

questions.question: The sum of the lengths of the edges of a cube is equal to the perimeter of a square. If the numerical value of the volume of the cube is equal to the numerical value of the area of the square, then the length of one side of the square is:
questions.solution:
Let the edge of the cube and the side of the square be M and N respectively.

The sum of the lengths of the edges of a cube is equal to the perimeter of a square,

⇒ 12M = 4N

⇒ M = N/3

The numerical value of the volume of the cube is equal to the numerical value of the area of the square,

⇒ M³ = N²

Solving,

⇒ N³/27 = N²

⇒ N = 27

∴ Side of square = 27 units

questions.question: Work done by an object on the application of a force would be zero if the displacement of the object is:
questions.solution:

• Where W means work done, F is force and s is displacement.

• W = F × 0
 
• W = 0.

questions.question: Consider a planet whose mass and radius are both twice the mass and radius of Earth. The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the planet is n times that on Earth. The value of n is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Consider the mass of the earth as ‘M’ and the radius of the earth ‘R’.

Now we consider a planet twice the mass and radius of earth as 2M and 2R.

We know the earth g = GM/R² i.e. is g propto (M)/({{R²)}} where G is Universal Gravitational Constant. 

Let g1 is the acceleration due to gravity on earth and g2 is acceleration due to the gravity of another planet.

So g2/g1 = (2M/M) × (R/2R)²

According due to gravity on surface of planet is n times of earth we get g2 = g1(n)

Hence, the value n is ½.

the ratio of the number of marbles that Jairam and Menaja had was 7 : 18,

⇒ P : J = 10 : 7
